A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PET imaging has a high sensitivity for the detection of lung cancer and is useful in determining the need for biopsy, staging and management.
PET is a valuable adjunct to CT for the evaluation of indeterminate pulmonary abnormalities, and it has a high negative predictive value for benignity.
FDG-PET has a high sensitivity and specificity in the evaluation of patients with indeterminate lung lesions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of PET imaging in patients with lung nodules has been shown to decrease the number of invasive procedures performed and has been associated with improved cost-effectiveness.
the combination of FDG PET and CT is superior to CT alone for the detection of lung cancer.

PET is a powerful diagnostic tool in patients with lung lesions that have been identified by chest radiograph or CT and that the use of PET can reduce the number of unnecessary biopsies, reduce the number of surgical procedures and reduce the cost of patient care.
